An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.text:
I checked every line of the four spec sections against the code by reading it. I could not run anything: Bash was denied, so neither the smoke script nor the edge cases below were tested live. Most of the spec is implemented correctly.

**What matches the spec:**
- **Startup:** it checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then listens, in that order. `PORT` parsing is right: empty or unset means 3000, digits only, at most 65535, and `PORT=0` reports the port actually bound.
- **Data file:** `ENOENT` means no bookings. Anything else, including a directory (EISDIR), bad JSON or the wrong layout, writes `cannot read data file <name>` using the name as given and exits 1.
- **Saving:** the file is saved before the reply is sent, and `store` and `nextId` only change once the save has worked. Changes are queued and run one at a time, so overlapping bookings sent together get one 201 and 409s, and no id is reused.
- **Request handling:**
  - The whole body is read before any reply, 413 and 415 included.
  - Unexpected failures become 500 `internal error` and the server keeps running.
  - Paths are matched byte for byte, `?date` handling uses `URLSearchParams`, and the 404/405 split for `/api/bookings/...` is right.
- **Booking rules:** the order 415 → 413 → 400 → 409 is right, and the media-type parsing (ASCII case only, spaces and tabs trimmed) is right. The body is decoded so a leading byte order mark stays and makes the body invalid JSON. The 409 reports the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
- **Replies and page:** every message, status code and content type is exact, and `/` and `/app.js` are served with the right types.

**What is below the bar:**

1. **Size (house rule):** `createApp` at `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/server.mjs:191-321` is about 130 lines, well over the 50-line limit. Each inner function is small, but the factory itself breaks the rule and holds handlers, routing and error handling together.
2. **A bad `PORT` can produce more than one line.** Line 338 echoes the raw value, so `PORT=$'12\nab'` writes two lines to stderr. The spec says the server writes exactly one line.
3. **A failed save can damage the file.** `writeFile` (line 127) empties the file before writing. If the write fails partway (a full disk, for example), memory is unchanged but the file is left damaged, and the next start exits with `cannot read data file`. That breaks "nothing changes".
4. **A late server error would crash the process.** `server.once('error')` (line 349) only catches errors from `listen`. Any later `'error'` event on the server has no listener and would end the process.
5. **Minor duplication:** the 409 code sorts by start time itself instead of reusing a shared comparer, and two string-type checks are repeated.

Tests are n/a, as you asked. The overall of 8 is the average of the other seven scores. That misses your bar of 9, though no item is under 7.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 8 — cohesive helpers and frozen, replaced state, but `createApp` bundles state, all handlers, routing and error handling in one closure
naming: 9 — clear, consistent names (`fieldError`, `commit`, `serialize`, `MSG.*`)
duplication: 8 — 409 clash sort repeats start comparison; redundant `typeof` checks at lines 64-65
size: 7 — file is 357 lines (fine) but `createApp` spans about 130 lines, over the 50-line limit
errors: 8 — data-file and listen errors handled well and 500s leak nothing; bad PORT can print more than one line, failed save can leave the file damaged, only one `'error'` listener
tests: n/a — written by the testing section
security: 9 — no secrets, input validated at the boundary, body memory capped, no path traversal (static map is fixed)
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs; stdout carries only the listening line
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/server.mjs:191 split `createApp` into module-level functions (e.g. `listBookings(state, res, query)`, `createBooking(state, req, res, body)`, `deleteBooking(state, res, idText)`, `route(state, ...)`) that share a small state object holding `store`, `queue` and `dataPath`, so each function is under 50 lines
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/server.mjs:338 do not echo the raw value (or wrap it in `JSON.stringify(process.env.PORT)`) so stderr always gets exactly one line
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/server.mjs:127 write to a temp file in the same folder, then `rename` it over the data file, deleting the temp file on failure, so a failed save leaves the old file intact
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/server.mjs:349 after a successful listen, add a lasting `server.on('error', ...)` handler so a later server error cannot crash the process
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/server.mjs:241 replace the inline ternary sort with a named `byStart` comparer (or reuse `compareBookings`)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/server.mjs:64 drop the redundant `typeof body.room !== 'string'` check (`ROOMS.includes` covers it), and at line 65 let `isValidTitle` own the type check
